preamble: Raising and centralization of /a/ to the near-open central vowel [ɐ], above all in unstressed syllables. In Bulgarian [ɐ] is the unstressed allophone of /a/, so stress-contrasting pairs such as па̀ра [ˈparɐ] 'steam' and пара̀ [pɐˈra] 'coin' differ in which /a/ is raised. In European Portuguese unstressed /a/ is raised to [ɐ] (pagar [pɐˈɣaɾ]), and only [ɐ] occurs in final unstressed syllables (casa [ˈkazɐ]). Stressed /a/ is raised to [ɐ] as well before a nasal consonant that begins the next syllable (cama [ˈkɐmɐ] 'bed', ano [ˈɐnu] 'year'), a position where Brazilian Portuguese has nasalized [ɐ̃] and northern Portugal keeps [a]. In Moscow-standard Russian /a/ is [ɐ] in the syllable immediately before the stress and word-initially, and [ə] further from the stress; St Petersburg speech has [ʌ] in the same position.

examples.note: Minimal pair with пара̀ 'coin': stress decides which /a/ surfaces as [ɐ].

examples.from: pagar 'to pay', unstressed a (cf. stressed paga [ˈpaɣɐ])
examples.note: Cruz-Ferreira (1995) writes the unstressed vowel as /ɐ/ (pɐˈgar).
The stressed vowel stays [a]; only the final unstressed vowel is raised.

Mateus & d'Andrade (2000), as cited in Wikipedia's Portuguese phonology, give the position before a nasal consonant as one of the three where stressed [ɐ] occurs. Northern Portugal keeps /ˈka.mɐ/; Brazilian Portuguese has /ˈkɐ̃.mɐ/.
The past falámos 'we spoke', analysed as two /a/ in crasis, keeps [a]: [fɐˈlamuʃ].
